- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp moves; adjust downward or dampen momentum.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days) — cap forecast rise after 2-3 consecutive high sentiment days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 days of high prices followed by drop), model often fails to correct — reduce forecast by 1-2% per day of overextension.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5-7 days) — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows strong divergence (e.g., 10+ days of +1.00 vs. 0.33), model may misalign with sentiment — adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction, not just price history.
